---
title: "UVP Lipids and morphotraits analysis"
author: "Patrick Pata"
date: "2025-01-21"
output: html_document
---

This is the preliminary exploration of the contents of the UVP5 and UVP6 copepod data. The morphological traits estimated within ecotaxa are analyzed with the metadata. The prosome and lipid content segmented as the training dataset and as the result of the fastai image segmentation pipeline are additionally used as trait information.

Data preparation tasks:
1. Load the UVP5/6 metadata file that include the morphological traits.
2. Based on the file of image masks, label which images have prosome and lipid masks.
3. For the manually segmented images, get the number of pixels assigned prosome or lipid and convert to mg.
4. For the ML segmented imaged, get number of pixels assigned prosome or lipid and convert to mg. 
5. Also calculate the major axis and minor axis lengths of the segmented prosome and lipids.

(3-5 might be done in Python when processing the ML segmentation results)


Data analysis tasks:
A. Sampling information
- open TSV files and filter columns
- visualize the spatial 3D and temporal distribution of the image data
- classify images according to depth or environmental zones

B. Segmentation model accuracy
- compare the pixels and mg differences between the manual and ML segmentations
- make sure to separate which images were used as training or test data


C. Morphological traits
- do ordinations and similar analysis as with Laure's UVP5 greenedge analysis
- estimate lipid content from biovolume using published allometric scaling relationships

D. Prosome size and lipid traits
- scaling relationship between prosome and lipid content, by area and by length
- plot the spatial distribution of the lipid content


E. Lipid content and morphological traits
- compare the major and minor axis lengths (and resulting biovolume) of the segmented images with that of the ecotaxa morphotraits
- find correlations between morphotraits and lipid content
- find relationships between morphotraits and if an image has a segmented (visible) lipid sac. I.e. are there predictors for these based on the ecotaxa data
- project the prosome and lipid content traits against the ordination of the morphological traits

# Load data and libraries

Important: LOKI metadata does not include longitude and latitude. This could be extracted by matching the files from arcticnet2013 ecotaxa projects

! The arcticenet2015 loki images are not yet in

Note that images here only copepods labelled with visible lipids.
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
#devtools::install_github("jiho/morphr", force =T)
# library("morphr")

source("../Vilgrain2021/lib/kaiser_guttman.R")

uvp5_ge_side <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/UVP5_greenedge/ecotaxa_export_149_20241018_1551.tsv", sep = '\t', header = TRUE)
uvp5_ge_top <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/UVP5_greenedge/ecotaxa_export_149_20241018_1553.tsv", sep = '\t', header = TRUE)
uvp5_ge <- bind_rows(uvp5_ge_side, uvp5_ge_top)
rm(uvp5_ge_side, uvp5_ge_top)


uvp6_de_side <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/UVP6_darkedge/ecotaxa_export_5108_20241018_1521.tsv", sep = '\t', header = TRUE)
uvp6_de_top <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/UVP6_darkedge/ecotaxa_export_5108_20241018_1518.tsv", sep = '\t', header = TRUE)
uvp6_de <- bind_rows(uvp6_de_side, uvp6_de_top)
rm(uvp6_de_side, uvp6_de_top)

# Only "Calanus" so far
uvp6_amund <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/UVP6_amundsen2023/Calanus/ecotaxa_export_10101_20250117_1943.tsv",sep = '\t', header = TRUE)
# filter columns?

# Only copepods with visible lipid sac
loki <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/LOKI_for_prosome_segmentation/ecotaxa_export_2331_20241009_1551.tsv", sep = '\t', header = TRUE)



# Column names are not exactly the same for all files. Determine which metadata is found in each file
meta <- data.frame(instrument = "uvp5_ge",
                   cnames = colnames(uvp5_ge)) %>% 
  bind_rows(data.frame(instrument = "uvp6_de",
                   cnames = colnames(uvp6_de))) %>% 
  bind_rows(data.frame(instrument = "uvp6_amund",
                       cnames = colnames(uvp6_amund))) %>% 
  bind_rows(data.frame(instrument = "loki",
                       cnames = colnames(loki))) %>%
  
  # Create a wide table of column names and corresponding datasets
  mutate(iscol = 1) %>% 
  group_by(cnames) %>% 
  mutate(ndata = sum(iscol)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = instrument, values_from = iscol, values_fill = NA) %>% 
  arrange(-ndata)

meta.all <- meta %>% 
  filter(ndata == max(ndata))

meta.uvp <- meta %>% 
  filter(ndata >= 3) %>% 
  filter(uvp6_amund == 1)


# LOKI2013 an UVP6_DE annotated and predicted prosome and lipid results
prosome_uvp6 <- read.csv("data/prediction_results_uvp6deamund_prosome.csv",
                         header = TRUE)
lipid_uvp6 <- read.csv("data/prediction_results_uvp6de_lipid.csv",
                         header = TRUE)

prosome_loki <- read.csv("data/prediction_results_loki2013_prosome.csv",
                         header = TRUE)
lipid_loki <- read.csv("data/prediction_results_loki2013_lipid.csv",
                         header = TRUE)
```

# Explore the morphospace from the UVP data

18 Morphological descriptors (Gorsky et al. 2010)
Size	Major = primary axis of an ellipse fitted on the object
	Minor = secondary axis of an ellipse fitted on the object
	Area = object area (i.e. number of pixels belonging to the object)
	Feret = distance between the 2 further points along object’s perimeter
	Perim. = perimeter length of the object
Shape	Circ. = circularity measure = (4*π*area)/perim., 1 = circle, 0 = line.
	Elongation = major/minor, 1 = circular >1 = elongated
	Thickr = Thickness ratio, relation between the maximum thickness of an object and the average thickness of the object excluding the maximum (Romagnan et al. 2016)
	Ver.Sym. = bilateral symmetry index
	Ver.Sym.2 = bilateral symmetry index taking into account only 75% of the darker pixels)
Transparency	Mean.grey = average grey value within the object ; sum of the grey values of all pixels in the object divided by the number of pixels (low = dark objects, high = clear objects)
	Med.grey = median grey value within the object
	Hist.grey 75% = grey level value at 75% of the normalized cumulative histogram of grey levels
	Sdev.grey = standard deviation of the grey value used to generate the mean grey value
	Skew.grey = skewness of the histogram of grey level values
Complexity	Perim./Major = Refers to both complexity (high values if the perimeter is particularly complex for an object of a given size) and circularity (round objects have a high perimeter/diameter ratio).
	Perim./Feret = same interpretation
	Fractal = fractal dimension of perimeter (Bérubé and Jébrak 1999)


```{r}
uvp.img <- uvp5_ge %>% 
  select(meta.uvp$cnames) %>% 
  mutate(instrument = "uvp5_ge") %>% 
  bind_rows(uvp6_de %>% 
              select(meta.uvp$cnames) %>% 
              mutate(instrument = "uvp6_de") ) %>% 
  bind_rows(uvp6_amund %>% 
              select(meta.uvp$cnames) %>% 
              mutate(instrument = "uvp6_amund") ) %>% 
  relocate(instrument) %>% 
  distinct(object_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Subset of metadata information, columns renamed
uvp.meta <- uvp.img %>% 
  select(object_id, instrument,
         lat = object_lat, lon = object_lon, depth = object_depth_min,
         date = object_date, time = object_time,
         annotation = object_annotation_category, sample_id, sample_cruise)

# Zooprocess morphological descriptors
# 18 traits were used in the Vilgrain et al. (2021) analysis
# zf <- select(z, Major, Minor, Perim., Feret, Area, Elongation ,
#              Ver.Sym., Ver.Sym.2, Circ., Thickr , Mean.grey, Med.grey,
#              "Hist.grey 75%", Sdev.grey, Skew.grey, Fractal,
#              "Perim./Feret", "Perim./Major")

uvp.morpho <- uvp.img %>% 
  select(object_id,
         Major = object_major, Minor = object_minor, Perim. = object_perim.,
         Feret = object_feret, Area = object_area, Elongation = object_elongation,
         Ver.Sym. = object_symetriev, Ver.Sym.2 = object_symetrievc, 
         Circ. = object_circ., Thickr = object_thickr, 
         Mean.grey = object_mean, Med.grey = object_median,
         `Hist.grey 75%` = object_histcum3, 
         Sdev.grey = object_stddev, Skew.grey = object_skew,
         Fractal = object_fractal, 
         `Perim./Feret` = object_perimferet,
         `Perim./Major` = object_perimmajor) %>% 
  remove_rownames() %>% 
  column_to_rownames("object_id")


pca <- FactoMineR::PCA(as.matrix(uvp.morpho), graph = FALSE)
# Note can weigh rows based on concentration

plot(pca, label = "var")
plot(pca, choix="var", axes = c(1,2))
plot(pca, choix="var", axes = c(3,4))

summary(pca)

# selection of axis :
kaiser_guttman(pca)


```


# Explore the accuracy of annotated prosome and lipids
```{r}
# LOKI images

# The analysis of the Maps et al. 2023 paper
meta.lipidsPaper <- read.csv("data/Maps2023_metadata_full.csv") %>% 
  mutate(data_use = if_else(is_valid == "True", "test", "train"))

ggplot(meta.lipidsPaper, aes(x = copepod_area_pixels,
                      y = IoU, color = data_use)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = .80, linetype = "dashed", color = "orange") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = .90, linetype = "longdash", color = "orange") +
  geom_smooth() +
  ggtitle(paste0("Maps et al. 2023 lipid results, IoU = ", 
                 sprintf("%.1f",mean(meta.lipidsPaper$IoU))))

ggplot(meta.lipidsPaper, aes(x = (copepod_mass_annotated - copepod_mass_pred),
                             fill = data_use)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  xlab("difference in mass (mg)") +
  ggtitle(paste0("Maps et al. 2023 results, RMSE = ", 
                 sprintf("%.3f", sqrt(mean(meta.lipidsPaper$copepod_mass_annotated -
                                             meta.lipidsPaper$copepod_mass_pred)^2)),
                 " mg"))
```

# Relate lipid content with morphospace (use annotated for now)
```{r}
uvp6_lipid_prosome <- prosome_uvp6 %>% 
  select(directory, filename, prosome_pixels_annotated, prosome_mass_annotated) %>% 
  left_join(lipid_uvp6 %>% 
              select(filename, lipid_pixels_annotated, lipid_mass_annotated),
            by = "filename") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(lipid_pixels_annotated)) %>%  # if only those images with lipid annotations
  # calculate lipid fullness based on pixels
  mutate(lipidfullness = lipid_pixels_annotated / prosome_pixels_annotated * 100) %>% 
  # create object_id column to match the ecotaxa export data
  mutate(object_id = str_remove(filename,".png"))
  

ggplot(uvp6_lipid_prosome) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = lipidfullness))
  

# subset of the ecotaxa export data with adjusted column names
uvp6_de_sub <- uvp6_de %>% 
  distinct(object_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  select(object_id, 
         lat = object_lat, lon = object_lon, depth = object_depth_min,
         date = object_date, time = object_time,
         annotation = object_annotation_category, sample_id, sample_cruise,
         
         Major = object_major, Minor = object_minor, Perim. = object_perim.,
         Feret = object_feret, Area = object_area, Elongation = object_elongation,
         # Ver.Sym., Ver.Sym.2, 
         Circ. = object_circ., Thickr = object_thickr, 
         # Mean.grey, Med.grey,
         # "Hist.grey 75%", Sdev.grey, Skew.grey, 
         Fractal = object_fractal, 
         `Perim./Feret` = object_perimferet,
         `Perim./Major` = object_perimmajor) 
  


# add morphotrait information
uvp6_lipid_morpho <- uvp6_lipid_prosome %>% 
  left_join(uvp6_de_sub, by = "object_id")


ggplot(uvp6_lipid_morpho, aes(x = lipid_mass_annotated, y = Perim.)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = depth)) +
  geom_smooth()

ggplot(uvp6_lipid_morpho, aes(x = lipidfullness, y = Perim.)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = depth)) +
  geom_smooth()


ggplot(uvp6_lipid_morpho, aes(x = lipidfullness, y = Area)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Elongation)) +
  geom_smooth()
```
